theory.intro: A site plan, survey or map is drawn to a stated scale. Convert each measured length to its real length first, then find the perimeter or area from those real lengths. Where a boundary is curved, estimate the area with the Trapezoidal rule.
facts: At a scale of $1:n$, $\text{real length}=\text{plan length}\times n$.
Area scales by $n^{2}$, not by $n$, so at $1:200$ one square centimetre on the plan is $40\,000$ square centimetres in real life.
The safest method is to convert every length to real life first, then apply the ordinary area formula.
$1\text{ m}^{2}=10\,000\text{ cm}^{2}$, so convert square centimetres to square metres by dividing by $10\,000$.
Floor plans usually give lengths in millimetres, so divide by $1000$ to get metres.
An **offset** is a perpendicular distance measured from the straight baseline out to the curved boundary.
Applying the rule to several equal strips and adding the results gives a closer estimate of the area.
steps: Convert each measured length on the plan to its real length using the scale
Find the perimeter or area from the real lengths, using the Trapezoidal rule for a curved boundary
State the answer in the unit the question asks for

foundation.question_text:
A plan of a rectangular courtyard is drawn to a scale of $1:200$.
On the plan the courtyard measures $5$ cm by $3$ cm.
Find the real perimeter of the courtyard, in metres.

A survey plan is drawn to a scale of $1:500$.
A triangular garden bed on the plan has a base of $4$ cm and a perpendicular height of $5$ cm.
Find the real area of the garden bed, in square metres.

A plan is drawn to a scale of $1:200$.
A rectangular room on the plan has an area of $12\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Find the real area of the room, in square metres.

A floor plan gives all measurements in millimetres.
A rectangular verandah measures $4800$ mm by $2500$ mm.
Find the area of the verandah, in square metres.

foundation.solution_text:
$h=5\times1000$
$=5000\text{ cm}$
$=50\text{ m}$
$d_{f}=3\times1000=3000\text{ cm}=30\text{ m}$
$d_{l}=4\times1000=4000\text{ cm}=40\text{ m}$
$A\approx\dfrac{50}{2}(30+40)$
$\approx25\times70$
$\approx1750\text{ m}^{2}$

foundation.question_text:
A survey plan is drawn to a scale of $1:400$.
A triangular reserve has sides measuring $3$ cm, $4$ cm and $5$ cm on the plan.
Find the real perimeter of the reserve, in metres.

development.solution_text:
$8\times200=1600\text{ cm}=16\text{ m}$
$5\times200=1000\text{ cm}=10\text{ m}$
$3\times200=600\text{ cm}=6\text{ m}$
$2\times200=400\text{ cm}=4\text{ m}$
$A=16\times10-6\times4$
$=160-24$
$=136\text{ m}^{2}$

$h=2\times2000=4000\text{ cm}=40\text{ m}$
$2\times2000=4000\text{ cm}=40\text{ m}$
$3.5\times2000=7000\text{ cm}=70\text{ m}$
$3\times2000=6000\text{ cm}=60\text{ m}$
$A\approx\dfrac{40}{2}(40+70)+\dfrac{40}{2}(70+60)$
$\approx20\times110+20\times130$
$\approx2200+2600$
$\approx4800\text{ m}^{2}$

development.question_text:
A plan of a park is drawn to a scale of $1:2500$.
The real park has an area of $50\,000\text{ m}^{2}$.
Find the area of the park on the plan, in square centimetres.

A floor plan gives all measurements in millimetres.
A rectangular room measures $5400$ mm by $3600$ mm.
Find the perimeter of the room, in metres.

On an aerial photograph, a scale bar of length $2$ cm represents $50$ m. A rectangular paddock on the photograph measures $6$ cm by $4.5$ cm.
Find the real area of the paddock, in square metres.
development.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }50\div2=25\text{ m}$
$\text{length}=6\times25=150\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=4.5\times25=112.5\text{ m}$
$A=150\times112.5$
$=16\,875\text{ m}^{2}$

development.question_text:
A rectangular pool measures $4$ cm by $2.5$ cm on a plan and has a real area of $250\text{ m}^{2}$.
Find the scale of the plan, in the form $1:n$.

mastery.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }84\div6=14\text{ m}$
$h=84\text{ m}$
$d_{f}=2\times14=28\text{ m}$
$d_{l}=3.5\times14=49\text{ m}$
$A\approx\dfrac{84}{2}(28+49)$
$\approx42\times77$
$\approx3234\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
A rectangular deck measures $7.5$ cm by $4$ cm on a plan drawn to a scale of $1:80$.
Decking boards cost $\$68$ per square metre.
Find the cost of the decking boards for the deck.

A floor plan in millimetres shows a rectangular kitchen $4200$ mm by $3000$ mm, containing a rectangular island bench $1800$ mm by $900$ mm.
Find the floor area that is not covered by the island bench, in square metres.

A map is drawn to a scale of $1:5000$.
The curved eastern boundary of a property is surveyed from a straight baseline using two strips, each $1.5$ cm wide on the map, with offsets of $1.2$ cm, $2$ cm and $1.6$ cm.
Use two applications of the Trapezoidal rule to estimate the area of the property, in square metres.
